note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: DRAG attack on split inference: guided-diffusion method, its extension, and results against models, defenses and shuffling

nodes.name: Split inference exposes IRs
nodes.description: In split inference the client model maps private input x to an intermediate representation (IR) h = fc(x) that is sent to a cloud server, so an adversary can try to reconstruct x from h.

nodes.name: Foundation-model SI privacy unexplored
nodes.description: Existing data reconstruction attacks mostly target small CNN classifiers (e.g. ResNet18); the privacy risks of vision transformers and foundation models in split inference are largely unexplored.

nodes.name: DRAG uses LDM prior with guidance
nodes.description: DRAG reconstructs inputs by performing guided diffusion on a pre-trained latent diffusion model's image prior, using DSG-based guidance from the distance between fc(x) and the target IR, gradient clipping with Adam, and self-recurrence to handle non-convex fc.

nodes.name: DRAG++ adds inverse-network init
nodes.description: DRAG++ initializes DRAG with a coarse reconstruction from an auxiliary inverse network trained on public data, noised at a small timestep t = sT.

nodes.name: DRAG beats baselines at deep layers
nodes.description: On CLIP-ViT-B/16 and DINOv2 without defenses, DRAG consistently outperforms rMLE, LM and GLASS at deeper split points, while rMLE and LM are competitive only at shallow split points.

nodes.name: DRAG++ improves perceptual quality
nodes.description: On CLIP-ViT-B/16, DRAG++ gives higher LPIPS and DINO scores than the inverse network alone and DRAG at split points beyond layer 3, with only a slight MS-SSIM loss relative to the inverse network.

nodes.name: Generalizes out of distribution
nodes.description: DRAG and DRAG++ also reconstruct out-of-distribution aerial images from the UCMerced LandUse dataset.

nodes.name: Defenses DISCO and NoPeek still fail
nodes.description: Input data can still be reconstructed by DRAG from CLIP-ViT-B/16 layer-12 IRs protected by DISCO (Config III) and NoPeek (Config VI), including against adaptive attacks.

nodes.name: Token shuffling defeats rMLE and LM
nodes.description: Under token shuffling and 50% token dropping on CLIP-ViT-B/16 layer 12, rMLE and LM fail to reconstruct images.

nodes.name: Token-order classifier partly undoes shuffling
nodes.description: A 2-layer MLP token-position classifier reaches 21.40% top-1 accuracy (average L1 distance 2.34) on ImageNet-1K, enabling reordering by the Hungarian algorithm.

nodes.name: GLASS and DRAG degrade but retain features under shuffling
nodes.description: Under shuffling, GLASS and DRAG reconstructions degrade, but some images still retain key features of the original inputs.

isolated_nodes.name: ViTs have token order invariance
isolated_nodes.description: ViTs exhibit token order invariance, absent in CNNs, which makes token shuffling a straightforward defense for tasks like classification.

isolated_nodes.name: Privacy risk calls for stronger defenses
isolated_nodes.description: The results show large vision foundation models in split inference are vulnerable, posing risks to applications like domestic robots and cyber-physical systems, and call for more robust privacy protection.

isolated_nodes.name: Task differs from prior guided diffusion
isolated_nodes.description: Unlike earlier guided-diffusion tasks, DRAG faces non-convex client models, deployed defenses forcing adversarial settings, and client-embedded randomness.

structural_reasoning: Split inference exposure and the research gap motivate DRAG; its method yields results across settings. Token-shuffling analysis connects to the shuffled-reconstruction result. Remaining claims are isolated.
